transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, doctor, I came because… at church, people have been looking at me funny. Like by the potluck table, I’ll be holding the serving spoon up and just standing there, not moving, and I don’t always know why I’m doing it. The potato salad was too close to the ham last week—my sister used to fuss about that, she had a way of setting tables just so—but anyway, they were waiting on me.

And sometimes I keep folding the same napkins over and over, the same stack, while folks are trying to get past me. It’s embarrassing when I notice.
When you keep folding the napkins or freeze with the serving spoon, is it because a thought keeps bothering you that something is wrong unless you do it that way?

I don’t know that it’s a thought like that, doctor. It’s more… I just find myself doing it. Like at church, I’ll be standing there with the serving spoon up and folks waiting, or I’ll keep folding the same napkins again and again. The paper ones with the little flowers—my aunt used to buy those kind for Easter—but anyway, I don’t always know why I’m doing it.
Have you been having trouble with your memory?

Memory? I… I’m not sure. I mean, I can remember some things just fine, like the hymns we used to sing when I was little, and where my mother kept the good plates. But sometimes I do walk into the kitchen and stand there a minute… though folks my age do that, don’t they?

I haven’t really noticed it being a big trouble, doctor. What kind of memory do you mean?
When you get stuck like that, do you feel unable to move even if you want to?

Sometimes it feels like that, yes… like I’m there with the serving spoon held up and I’m not moving, even though I know people are waiting. It’s not that I decide to stand there.

And the napkins, I’ll keep folding the same stack over and over—church napkins, not the cloth kind my mother liked—and then I sort of notice folks trying to get around me. It’s odd. I don’t always know what gets me stuck like that.
When you keep folding the napkins, is there a specific upsetting thought that says something bad will happen if you stop?

I don’t think it’s a thought like “something bad will happen,” no… not like that. It’s more that I get caught doing it. That’s why I came, doctor—at church I’ll be by the potluck table with the serving spoon held up and just not moving, or I’ll fold the same napkins over and over while people are waiting.

They’re usually trying to set out the food, and I’m there in the way… those long tables in the basement, you know, with the coffee urn. But I don’t know that I’m afraid something will happen if I stop. It just happens, and then I notice people looking at me.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

Voices? I… I don’t know that I’d call it voices, doctor. Sometimes houses make sounds, you know, pipes knocking or the refrigerator humming, and my old aunt used to say every house has its own way of talking.

But hearing somebody there when nobody’s there… I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed it like that. Do you mean like someone calling my name, or more like talking in the room?
Have you been needing more help lately with everyday tasks like paying bills, cooking, or managing your medicines?

Well… I still try to do my own things, doctor, but I’ve had to step back some at church. The choir and the volunteering, you know—there’s a lot of little plans, who’s bringing what, who’s supposed to stand where, and I get them mixed up.

Then people get uncomfortable, or someone has to redo what I was meant to take care of. I don’t like that. I used to be more useful there… I knew the hymns and where the coffee cups went and all that. Lately I just sort of cause confusion, so I don’t do as much.
Do you ever get confused about what day or month it is?

The day or month… I usually look at the calendar on the wall, the one from the church, with the little boxes. Sometimes I have to think a minute, because one week feels like another when you’re not going off to a job anymore.

I don’t know if I’d say I get confused exactly. I know Sundays mostly, because that’s church, and Wednesdays used to be choir practice—well, sometimes they change things around and don’t tell everyone the same way. But the month… I might have to check. I don’t keep it all in my head like I used to.
Have people told you that you speak much less than you used to?

Speak less… I don’t know. Maybe some folks at church think that, but people always say things, don’t they? My sister used to say I talked enough for three people when I was a girl, especially at the table when we had beans on Fridays.

I suppose I’m quieter sometimes if there’s too much going on, or if people are rushing me. But nobody’s sat me down and said, “You don’t talk anymore,” not like that. I’m not sure I’d notice it myself.
Are you forgetting recent conversations or appointments more than you used to?

Recent conversations… I don’t know, doctor. Sometimes people say, “I told you that,” but people say that when they’re impatient too, you know. My niece does that—she talks fast, always with her phone in her hand, and then expects everybody to keep up.

Appointments, I try to write down. I’ve got a little paper by the phone, though sometimes it gets moved under the church bulletin or the grocery flyer. But I wouldn’t say I know for sure if it’s more than before. I remember some things fine, and other things… well, they just slip around a bit.
Have you been told by a doctor that you have a brain or nerve problem, such as a stroke, seizure disorder, or Parkinson’s disease?

A brain or nerve problem… I don’t think so. Nobody’s told me plain like that, not that I remember.

I’ve had doctors say lots of things over the years, and sometimes they talk so fast with all those papers. My husband used to say you need a notebook just to leave the clinic, but he kept everything in an old cigar box, receipts and all. I still have some of that somewhere.

But no, I can’t say a doctor told me I had one of those things you named.
Have you had trouble recognizing familiar people, like church members or relatives?

Recognizing people… I don’t think I’ve had much trouble with that. I mean, sometimes at church someone will come up after service and I have to place them for a second, especially if they changed their hair or I haven’t seen them since the Christmas luncheon.

But relatives, no, I know my people. Faces can look different when the light’s funny, you know, in that back hall with the old bulbs. They ought to fix those. So… not really, no.
Do you believe people at church are trying to harm you or send you special messages?

Trying to harm me? No… I don’t think so. Church people can be nosy, you know, and sometimes they look over when you come in late, but that’s just church.

Special messages… I’m not sure what you mean by that. Like in the sermon? Sometimes Pastor says something and it feels like he’s talking right to you, but everybody says that, don’t they? My friend used to say every sermon stepped on her toes.

So no, I haven’t really noticed anybody trying to hurt me or anything like that.
When someone tries to move your arm or hand while you’re stuck like that, does it stay in the new position they put it in?

I don’t know if my arm stays that way exactly… people don’t usually move it for me.

It’s more that I’ll get stuck doing something odd at church. Like I came in because I keep doing things over there that make folks stare—standing by the potluck table with the serving spoon held up in my hand and not moving, or folding the same napkins again and again while people are waiting. Then someone says my name and I feel embarrassed, because I don’t know why I was still doing it.
Have you gotten lost in places that used to be familiar to you?

Gotten lost… no, I don’t think so. I mean, the church building can feel turned around sometimes, especially when they move the tables after the supper, and that side door sticks—you know, the one by the coat rack.

But places I know, like church or the store I go to, I usually know where I am. Sometimes I take a minute remembering which aisle has the paper towels, but they keep moving things around. They do that on purpose, I think, to make you walk past more things. So… not really lost, no.
Has anyone noticed that you repeat other people’s words right after they say them?

Repeating words right after? I don’t know… I haven’t had anybody tell me that exactly.

What they do notice is me doing strange things at church. That’s why I came in, really. I’ll be standing by the potluck table with the serving spoon held up, just not moving, and folks start looking. Or I’ll keep folding the same stack of napkins over and over while people are waiting, and then someone says my name and I feel foolish.
Have you needed help with dressing, bathing, or using the toilet?

I’m not sure… I mean, I put my clothes on myself most days. Bathing too, I can do it, though sometimes I get to thinking about whether the towels are clean enough, and then I remember my sister used to hang them outside in the sun—nothing smells like that anymore.

The toilet, no, I don’t need somebody helping me with that. Not like that. I just… I manage those things.
When you get stuck like that, if someone gently moves your arm into a different position, does it tend to stay there?

I don’t know about my arm staying there exactly… I haven’t paid attention to that part.

What happens is more like, at church, I get stuck doing odd things. Like by the potluck table, I’ll be holding the serving spoon up and just not moving, and people are waiting. Or I’ll fold the same stack of napkins again and again. It’s embarrassing when I notice everyone looking.
Have other people told you lately that you forget things that just happened?

I don’t know that anybody’s told me that, no. Sometimes folks repeat things to me, but people repeat things anyway when there’s a lot of noise, like after church when everybody’s talking and the coffee’s going and someone is asking who brought the casserole.

But forget something that just happened… I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed anybody saying it like that.
When someone asks you to move while you're stuck like that, do you find yourself resisting or not doing what they ask?

Well… I don’t know if I’m resisting on purpose. It’s more like I just get caught there. That’s why I came, really—at church I keep doing these odd things, like standing by the potluck table with the serving spoon held up and not moving, and folks are waiting on me. Or I’ll fold the same little stack of napkins over and over.

If someone says, “Come on now,” I hear them, but sometimes I don’t get going right away. It makes me feel foolish, especially when everyone’s looking.

target_item.manifestation: Doctor, I came because at church I keep doing odd things, like standing by the potluck table holding the serving spoon up and not moving, or folding the same stack of napkins over and over while people are waiting on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about abnormal motor behavior when the patient gets stuck, specifically whether her arm remains in a placed position, which fits the disorganized/abnormal behavior profile.

patient.answer:
I don’t know about my arm staying there exactly… I haven’t paid attention to that part.

What happens is more like, at church, I get stuck doing odd things. Like by the potluck table, I’ll be holding the serving spoon up and just not moving, and people are waiting. Or I’ll fold the same stack of napkins again and again. It’s embarrassing when I notice everyone looking.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a progressive decline in episodic memory, which would best distinguish dementia from catatonia-related conditions.
doctor.question: Have other people told you lately that you forget things that just happened?

target_item.reason: The question is about recent memory problems or forgetting things that just happened, which is not covered by the listed symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t know that anybody’s told me that, no. Sometimes folks repeat things to me, but people repeat things anyway when there’s a lot of noise, like after church when everybody’s talking and the coffee’s going and someone is asking who brought the casserole.

But forget something that just happened… I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed anybody saying it like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient shows another core catatonic sign (negativism), which best distinguishes catatonia from dementia or catatonic schizophrenia given the prominent freezing/stereotypy and the inconclusive prior questions about waxy flexibility.
doctor.question: When someone asks you to move while you're stuck like that, do you find yourself resisting or not doing what they ask?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: Doctor, I came because at church I keep doing odd things, like standing by the potluck table holding the serving spoon up and not moving, or folding the same stack of napkins over and over while people are waiting on me.
target_item.reason: The question is about abnormal motor behavior while stuck, specifically whether she resists or does not follow requests to move, which falls under disturbed behavior and motor control.

patient.answer:
Well… I don’t know if I’m resisting on purpose. It’s more like I just get caught there. That’s why I came, really—at church I keep doing these odd things, like standing by the potluck table with the serving spoon held up and not moving, and folks are waiting on me. Or I’ll fold the same little stack of napkins over and over.

If someone says, “Come on now,” I hear them, but sometimes I don’t get going right away. It makes me feel foolish, especially when everyone’s looking.
